summary: Nicola Di Cosmo works in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. Educated at Indiana State and Indiana University (PhD ~1991), he held posts at Harvard, Canterbury, Columbia, and the Institute for Advanced Study (~2003).

Nicolaas Johannes Krom was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (1913–1916) and held a professorship at Leiden University (1919, 1925–1945).
Nicolaas van Wijk was a linguist who studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1898–1903) and Moscow State University (~1903–1904). He took up a post at Leiden University in 1913.
Nicolas Morrissey specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Gregory Schopen and holds a post at the University of Georgia.

Nicolas Revire is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Silpakorn University and was supervised by Claudine Bautze-Picron, Peter Skilling, and Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h. He held a post at Thammasat University (attested 2016–2017).

Nicolas Tournadre works in linguistics and Tibetology. After doctoral studies under Claude Hagège at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1988–1992), he held posts at INALCO (~1995–2004), Aix-Marseille I (~2004–2011), and Aix-Marseille University (~2004).
Nicole Baden is an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Richard Baker, whom she succeeded in 2024.

Nicole Vandier-Nicolas worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She taught Chinese art at the École du Louvre and served as professor of Chinese civilization at INALCO (~1958–1976).

Niels Ludvig Westergaard was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Copenhagen, Bonn (under Christian Lassen), Paris, London, and Oxford, later serving as professor and Rektor at the University of Copenhagen.
Nigel Allan specialized in history, archaeology, and other fields. Succeeding Marianne Winder, he served as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust (attested 1993).

Niharranjan Ray worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Murari Chand College, Calcutta, UCL, and Leiden, he served as professor at the University of Calcutta (1946–1965) and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1965–1970).

Nika Jovic specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and Géza Bethlenfalvy, completing her Magistra der Philosophie (attested 2010).
Nikita Yakovlevich Bichurin worked in Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Kazan Theological Academy and held a post at the Département asiatique (~1826–1853).

Niklas Luhmann was a philosopher and sociologist who studied at the University of Freiburg (~1946–1949), Harvard (~1960–1961), and Bielefeld University. He spent his career as a professor at Bielefeld University (~1968–1993).

Nikolai Solmsdorf specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard and held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013).

Nina Mirnig is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She earned her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (-2010) and held posts at the University of Groningen, Austrian Academy of Sciences, and IKGA.

Ninian Smart was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. Educated at Glasgow, SOAS, Oxford, and Yale, he held major professorships at the University of Birmingham (1961), Lancaster University (1967–1982), and the University of California, Santa Barbara (1976–1998).

Nirajan Kafle works in Indology. He completed his doctorate at Leiden University under Peter C. Bisschop (-2015) and held posts at the Nepal Research Centre, University of Naples "L'Orientale", and Leiden University.
Niran Rajvamshi works in history, archaeology, and Indology. In 2018, he was attested with posts at the National Archives of Nepal and on the editorial board of Documenta Nepalica.
Nirmal C. Sinha was active as an editor, serving as Editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1978 and 1988).
